title: Dynamic Multimodality Imaging Assessment of Right Ventricular Thrombosis in a Middle-Aged Man with Lymphocytic Interstitial Pneumonia: The Additive Role of Tissue Doppler Imaging
content: Right ventricular thrombosis (RVT) is rarely detected in clinical practice. Depending on its etiology, RVT may originate from a deep venous thrombosis (type A) or in situ (type B). The type A is characterized by increased mobility and frequent pulmonary embolization, whereas the type B is nonmobile and is associated with significant right ventricular (RV) dilatation and dysfunction. The third RVT type is the type C, with intermediate characteristics between type A and type B. Herein, we present a case of type C RVT, originated in situ and complicated by subsegmental pulmonary embolism (PE), diagnosed in a 46-year-old man with acute-on-chronic respiratory failure secondary to acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease. He underwent a multimodality imaging assessment of the RV mass comprehensive of TTE, TEE, contrast-enhanced chest CT and LGE-CMR. During the clinical course, a serial echocardiographic assess-ment of the RV mass allowed to provide a dynamic evaluation of its features and cardiac hemodynamics. Conventional TTE was implemented with color-tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) and pulsed wave (PW) TDI to improve the visualization of RV mass and to objectively measure its mobility. The increased RVT mass peak antegrade velocity (>10 cm/s) was predictive of the subsequent RVT fragmentation and pulmonary embolization. In conclusion, color-TDI and PW-TDI may aid in the differential diagnosis of RV masses and may improve the prognostic risk stratification of patients with right-sided intracardiac masses.
